why: A real take, cut for a 12-year-old: Tom saves a login change in Zed; ClawReflex hands the save to Kimi in standard OpenClaw on Cerebras; Kimi proves the bug with an attack test (RED, checked against a hidden reference), writes a fix that is applied only after 8 of 8 tests pass (GREEN), and Zed reloads the fixed file. Then a live race of the same request on Cerebras and a GPU host. Every skipped wait is labelled with its length; the clip is built by clawreflex/cut.py from out/clawreflex/film/edl.json.

claim.footnote: *Cerebras' stated speed for Kimi. Measured here under hackathon load: 383 tokens/s.

intro.title: ClawReflex
intro.description: Every time you save, Kimi tries to break your code. If it gets in, it writes a fix, and keeps it only when every test passes.
